Hi Dana —

Quick answers from ops/security side and a proposed pattern attached. TL;DR: we can support the staged uplift and preserve tail-latency SLAs with the following config:

1) Billing band: the discount is retroactive for the month. If you hit >=3.5M tokens in a billing month, the lower per-token rate applies to the whole month's consumption. That reduces reconciliation overhead.

2) Burst credits: pooled monthly by tenant (not weekly). To accommodate weekly syncs we recommend a dedicated intermittent-burst allowance: set aside 200k tokens/month as "sync-burst" and implement a token-bucket with a 1-week replenishment window. This prevents one-off spikes from causing a hard throttle.

3) Rate limits and per-key semantics: our controls allow per-API-key limits layered on top of tenant-wide limits. Proposed defaults for FastCart: tenant-wide steady limit 90 rps, per-key limit 45 rps, burst window 20s (configurable). For the staged uplift we can set a trial increase to tenant-wide 110 rps for the first 30 days, observe KPIs, then commit to 120 rps after validation.

Fallback policy recommendation:
- Primary: route to full-precision model variant until saturation
- Soft-fallback: switch to quantized variant preserving API surface and reducing cost/latency impact
- Hard-fallback: queue with retry-after header (only if both variants exceeded)

Ops attachments: ops_note_throttle_pattern.txt (contains sample token-bucket math and runbook steps), and I'll push the per-route policy into a staging config for 2027-06-15.

Vanessa: CS-runbook action items below — will need a 30-min joint run-through with FastCart ops the week of 2027-06-14.

—Karthik
